correctness.rationale: For all positive real normalized gaps, the discharge derivative on each event-activity interval is a strictly concave quadratic times a positive exponential. The unique root of F(d)=2-d+4(1-d)exp(-d) controls its sign at the third arrival, while the global negative slope bound of the single response ensures a positive derivative one time unit after the third event. Exact sign tables force respectively 1,2,3 strict crests; both equality gaps handled. The embedded self-contained finite checker passed 2297 supplementary assertions; it is not used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest published mathematical finding determines the two-pulse three-reservoir regime; it does not imply a new two-crest interval below the single-pulse modal lag made possible by three equispaced impulses. Inspectable hydrology literature establishes the linear gamma-response kernel, multiple stochastic pulses, finite-duration storm simulations or one rectangular storm peak; none supplies the exact 1→2→3 crest-count transition. The review recognizes that generic mixture theory or inaccessible older work could contain equivalent coverage; best-evidence original, not independently certified.

value.rationale: The first threshold is a sharp natural resolution boundary for a three-event rainfall pulse train. It proves that a pair of storm inputs is insufficient to predict how three bursts merge at the outlet: a 3-stage catchment can display two genuine peaks at spacing 1.537805…<2, whereas two equal events cannot. The full classification gives an exact routing-model test benchmark and is not a routine one-parameter substitution or numerical experiment. It does not pretend empirical robustness near the thresholds.
